hook: True transparency is physically impossible because quantum decay turns photons into phonons, Scientific American reports.

sections.voiceover: True transparency is physically impossible because quantum decay turns photons into phonons, Scientific American reports.
sections.visual_cue: Macro shot of a clear glass prism refracting light into a rainbow.

sections.voiceover: On October 8, 2026, researchers Angelo Esposito, Alberto Nicolis, and Federico Piazza published an arXiv study explaining why. But how much light actually survives inside the clearest materials on Earth?
sections.visual_cue: Split-screen showing the arXiv manuscript text and a light beam passing through a crystal.

sections.voiceover: Ivan Smalyukh at the University of Colorado Boulder holds the Guinness record for the clearest material.
sections.visual_cue: Portrait of Ivan Smalyukh next to a laboratory setup at the University of Colorado Boulder.

sections.voiceover: Gels from the University of Colorado Boulder become light-absorbing when you apply a 30 cm layer.
sections.visual_cue: Graphic showing a 30 cm light-absorbing gel layer being measured with a digital caliper.

sections.voiceover: In a mathematically perfect superfluid, light travels the diameter of Earth before fading, Yahoo News reports.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of Earth from space with a fading beam of light passing through the planet.
